objectives: Say what anger is and where you feel it in your body.
Name the things that usually make you angry.
Calm yourself with five easy steps.
Use the calm words with a friend or a grown-up.
Know what to do when your anger is too big.
Say the hard thing with words instead of with your hands.

sections.body:
Anger is a big feeling. It comes fast, and it goes away slowly. When you are angry, your body is getting ready to fight or to run. That is useful, but it is not useful in a classroom or at home.

You can feel anger in different places. Your hands get hot. Your shoulders go up near your ears. Your tummy feels like there is a hot soup inside. Your face feels tight.

Your voice also changes. It becomes louder and higher. You might say things you do not mean. That is because the big feeling takes over the words.

Anger is not a bad feeling. Grown-ups get angry too. It tells you that something is not fair, or that you need help. The problem is not the feeling. The problem is what your hands and your mouth do while it is there.

Good anger helpers do one thing: they get the big feeling down to a small one first. Then they speak. The order matters. Body first, words second.
examples: I feel angry in my hands.
My voice got loud when I was angry.
sections.heading: What anger is, and where you feel it

sections.body:
Most anger comes from a few clear things. Knowing them helps you get ready.

**Something is not fair.** Your friend took your turn, or a younger one cut in line. Your body says that is wrong.

**Something is in your way.** A tower falls down. A puzzle will not fit. A ball goes out of the garden.

**You are tired or hungry.** A tired brain has no room left for patience. This is why everything feels like too much at the end of a long day.

**You are told no.** Your body wants it now. Grown-ups often say later, and later is hard to hear.

**Something was taken from you.** A pen, a seat, a game. Loss feels strong, even when it is small.

Notice what your anger is about. If you can say "I am angry because my turn was taken", you can do something about it. If you only say "I am angry", you are just as cross and no further along.
examples: I am angry because my turn was taken.
I am cross because this will not fit.
I am angry because I am hungry.
sections.heading: Why you feel angry

sections.body:
You cannot stop anger from arriving. But you can stop it from choosing what you do next. These five steps work every time, if you practise them when you are calm.

**One. Stop.** Do not hit, do not push, do not shout. Put your hands down by your sides or hold them together. Even standing still helps.

**Two. Breathe.** Take one slow breath in through your nose. Let it out through your mouth, like blowing out a candle. Do it three times. Your heart slows down while you breathe out.

**Three. Name it.** Say the feeling quietly to yourself. "I am angry." "I am frustrated." Naming a feeling makes it smaller.

**Four. Choose.** Think of one safe thing. Walk to the window. Count the blue things in the room. Drink some water. Pick the safe thing before the unsafe one.

**Five. Talk.** Now you can use words. Tell the person what happened, and tell them what you need. Words work much better from a calm body.

Practise the steps on easy days too. Try them when you are only a little cross. Then they will be there when you really need them.
examples: I am angry, so I am going to breathe.
I am angry because my turn was taken.
sections.heading: Five steps to calm down
steps: Stop. Hands down, no hitting and no shouting.
Breathe in slowly and blow out three times.
Choose one safe thing to do.
Talk about what happened and what you need.

sections.body:
These are the words for anger and for getting calm again. Learn them and you can tell somebody exactly what is inside you.

**Angry** is the strong feeling you get when something feels wrong or unfair.

**Frustrated** is a smaller angry feeling. It comes when you try and try and something still will not work.

**Calm down** means to bring your body back to quiet, so you can think and speak.

**Breathe** means to take air in slowly and let it out slowly. It is the fastest way to calm a big feeling.

Try each word out loud with a friend. Say the feeling, not the story. A friend understands "I am frustrated" straight away.
sections.heading: The angry and calm words, one by one

terms.example: I am angry about what happened.
terms.gloss: A strong feeling you get when something feels wrong or unfair.

terms.example: I am frustrated with this puzzle.
terms.gloss: A smaller angry feeling that comes when something still will not work.

terms.example: Let us calm down first, then talk.
terms.gloss: To bring your body back to quiet so you can think and speak.

terms.example: Breathe in, and blow out slowly.
terms.gloss: To take air in slowly and let it out slowly.

sections.body:
Sometimes the anger is so big that the five steps are not enough. That happens to everybody. Here is what to do then.

**Walk away.** Go to another part of the room, or go outside for one minute. Do not leave for ever. Just enough to get your body quiet.

**Get help.** Find a grown-up and say the words. "I am too angry to talk right now. Can you stay with me?" That is a strong sentence. Grown-ups like to hear it.

**Never hit.** Not a wall, not a table, not a person, not yourself. If your hands want to hit, squeeze a soft cushion instead. Or press your hands flat on the table.

**Take care of somebody.** Give your little brother a drink. Water your plant. Doing something kind uses up the extra energy in your body.

**Come back.** When the feeling is smaller, go back and finish the talk. You can still say what happened, even after you were cross. That is what grown-ups do.

If you are angry every single day, and it never goes away, tell a grown-up. There is help for that, and you do not have to carry it alone.
examples: I am too angry to talk right now.
Can you stay with me while I calm down?
I want to hit, so I will squeeze this cushion.
sections.heading: When the anger is too big for your body

sections.body:
A punch hurts for a moment. Mean words stay in your head for a long time. Children remember what other children said to them.

So when your anger is big, do not use your mouth as a weapon. Do not call somebody a bad name. Do not say things about a person that you would not say to their face.

Instead, say the truth in a way people can hear. "I am angry that you took my turn." "I did not like that." "Please stop, it hurts my feelings." These sentences are strong because they are clear.

And if somebody is angry with you, remember that their words are big too. Ask for an apology, and if it does not come, walk to a grown-up.

Being kind is not the same as being weak. A kind child can say no, can say stop, and can say very clearly that something is not acceptable.
examples: I am angry that you took my turn.
Please stop, it hurts my feelings.
sections.heading: Words can hurt more than hands

item.summary: Anger is a big feeling that comes fast and goes slow. After reading this, you can name what makes you angry, know where you feel it in your body, calm yourself in five steps, and choose words that do not hurt people.
item.title: What to Do When You Feel Angry
